Role-aware detection of broken access control in REST APIs

Results dashboard for the bachelor's thesis Automated Detection of Broken Access Control Vulnerabilities in REST APIs: A Role-Aware Testing Tool in JavaScript (Savonia UAS, Design Science Research). Every number is read from the archived experiment files.

Overview

Broken access control is the leading risk class in the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023). Two of its forms are hard for generic scanners, because they need to know who owns an object and which role may call a function.

BOLA: Broken Object Level Authorization (API1:2023)

The API checks that a caller is logged in but not whose object is being addressed. Alice changes /api/orders/17 to /api/orders/18 and reads Bob's order. The response is a normal 200 OK. Only knowing that order 18 belongs to Bob reveals the flaw.

BFLA: Broken Function Level Authorization (API5:2023)

A function meant for one role can be called by another. A regular user or a read-only guest calls DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} and it succeeds. Only the intended role policy shows that this 2xx is wrong.

Three approaches, compared on the same ground truth

Role-aware (this thesis)

Logs in as several accounts and generates cross-user and cross-role requests from the OpenAPI spec. An ownership-differential oracle then decides: it compares owner identifiers in the response and the owner's own response, and re-reads the state after writes and deletes.

Status-only baseline

Sends exactly the same requests from the same test plan, but flags any 2xx response to a request the policy forbids. The two scanner rows therefore differ only in the decision rule.

OWASP ZAP 2.17 (API scan)

The widely used open-source DAST tool, in its standard OpenAPI scan with one authenticated user. Its alerts are mapped to the same categories by a CWE mapping that was fixed before ZAP was run.

The benchmark

The benchmark is an Express API written for this thesis. Each flaw is switched by one ID (FLAWS=all for the vulnerable build, FLAWS=none for the patched build). True-negative patterns are correctly protected operations that still answer 2xx. They exist to separate a status-code oracle from an ownership-aware one. VAmPI, a third-party vulnerable API, is the external check.

Detection quality (RQ2)

Precision, recall, F1 and false-positive rate per approach, at the confirmed threshold. n/a means the metric is undefined because its denominator is zero (e.g. precision for a tool with no detections). It is never shown as 0.

Experiment status

As recorded in evaluation/README.md. Only executed experiments have results. Nothing on this page reports numbers for a planned experiment.

Validity notes. The benchmark and the tool were designed by the same author. The mitigations are VAmPI, the patched build, and a ground truth fixed before any tool run. The benchmark spec carries x-access-control policy annotations that real APIs usually lack, and the ablation without them (E6) is still planned. There are only 20 vulnerable cases on the benchmark (14 BOLA/BFLA) and 3 on VAmPI, so the raw counts matter more than the ratios. ZAP was used in its standard single-user API scan, without its manual Access Control Testing add-on.

Rebuild with node docs/dashboard/build.js. The page is self-contained: no network requests, no external scripts.
